nvitk.db.repo¶

High-level access to the on-disk dataset: catalog tables, measurements, assets, scans, and writes.

DataRepo resolves the dataset root (NVITK_DATASET_ROOT or the dataset/ tree next to the package), opens DatasetCatalog and SQLiteIndex, and exposes filtered queries with optional cohort scoping (see DEFAULT_COHORT_ID).

class nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo(root: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, *, use_sqlite: bool = True, auto_scaffold: bool = False)¶

Dataset-facing API: load tables, clinical/image measurements, assets, scans, and writes.

Queries prefer the SQLite index when use_sqlite is True and the index file exists; otherwise fall back to Parquet. Cohort filtering uses cohort_membership when present unless cohort_id=False (disable) or an explicit cohort id is passed.

Query clinical_measurements with variable resolution, optional value filters, and cohort scope.

Non-reserved filters keys are treated as variable ids with comparison specs (see apply_filters()). Set wide=False for long (tidy) form.

image(*, modality: str | None = None, variables: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, regions: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, atlas: str | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, wide: bool = True, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, pipeline: str | int | Iterable[str | int] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Query image_measurements with modality, regions, atlas (ASL or T1), pipeline selection, and filters.

When neither modality nor pipeline filters are given, rows are restricted to catalog default pipelines per modality where defined. Use atlas= with modality='asl' or modality='t1' to expand regions from a named atlas preset.

assets(*, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, modality: str | None = None, asset_type: str | None = None, resource_label: str | None = None, subject_uid: str | None = None, session_uid: str | None = None, pipeline_id: str | None = None, asset_slot: str | None = None, source: str | None = None, wide: bool = False, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, value: str = 'asset_path', get_image: bool = False, imread_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) → pandas.DataFrame | Any¶

Query the assets table; optionally pivot to one row per subject_uid (wide=True).

With get_image=True, resolve paths to nvitk.io.imageio.imread() jobs (NIfTI directories expand to multiple volumes; JSON sidecars are picked up when present). imread_kwargs is forwarded to imread; value selects the path column to read.

Assets as a wide table (one row per subject) by default; see assets().

scans(*, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, scan_uid: str | None = None, session_uid: str | None = None, subject_uid: str | None = None, scan_id: str | None = None, modality: str | None = None, orientation: str | None = None, resource_label: str | None = None, asset_slot: str | None = None, quality: str | None = None, series_description: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, path_column: str = 'local_cache_path', get_image: bool = False, asset_type: str | None = None, download_scan_path: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, xnat_config: nvitk.db.xnat_config.XnatConnectionConfig | None = None, skip_existing_download: bool = True, imread_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) → pandas.DataFrame | Any¶

Query the scans table; with get_image=True, load volumes from path_column.

Missing local paths can trigger XNAT download when xnat_config or env/profile resolves; use download_scan_path for a persistent cache directory. asset_type must be dicom or nifti for on-demand download; imread_kwargs passes through to imread.

Write df to the table’s Parquet file and refresh catalog schema metadata.

Set build_sqlite_index=True to rebuild the SQLite index for table after the write.

upsert_table(table: str, df: pandas.DataFrame, *, key_columns: list[str] | None = None, provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, build_sqlite_index: bool = False) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Append df to the existing table and drop duplicates on key_columns (default: manifest keys).

Always reads the current Parquet (not SQLite) so sequential upserts without an intervening index rebuild do not drop recently written rows.

Returns the combined frame after write_table().

_prepare_measurements(df: pandas.DataFrame, *, wide: bool, table_name: str, image_wide_single_variable: bool | None = None) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Resolve value_num/value_text into a unified value column and, if wide, pivot to one column per variable via _to_wide(); otherwise return the long frame with a fresh index.

_coerce_wide_measurement_dtypes(df: pandas.DataFrame, *, table_name: str) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Restore numeric dtypes on wide-pivoted measurement columns.

_resolve_measurement_values builds a single value series from value_num with a value_text fallback, which upcasts the whole series to object whenever any text variable is in the query. The subsequent pivot then leaves numeric variables (e.g. hematocrit) as object-dtype floats, and Patsy treats them as categoricals (Hematocrit[T.36.0], …). Coerce columns whose catalog value_kind is numeric back to float64.

_resolve_measurement_values(df: pandas.DataFrame) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Add a unified value column, preferring value_num and falling back to value_text row-wise where the numeric value is missing.

_to_wide(df: pandas.DataFrame, definition: nvitk.db.catalog.TableDefinition, *, image_wide_single_variable: bool | None = None) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Pivot a long measurement frame to wide form: one row per entity (wide_index_columns) and one column per composed key (region/variable/frame, see _compose_image_wide_keys() for image_measurements or _compose_wide_keys() otherwise), values from the value column.

_compose_wide_keys(df: pandas.DataFrame, key_columns: list[str]) → pandas.Series¶

Join key_columns per row with __ (skipping empty parts) to form wide-pivot column keys.

_relative_path(path: pathlib.Path) → str¶

path expressed relative to the dataset root, as a POSIX-style string for catalog storage.
